info.title: Ludo.ai API
info.description:
The Ludo.ai API enables you to generate game assets programmatically, including images, videos, 3D models, spritesheets, and audio.

# Getting Started

## Base URL
All API requests should be made to: `https://api.ludo.ai/api`

## Authentication
Include your API key in the `Authorization` header:
```
Authorization: ApiKey YOUR_API_KEY
```

## Models
Pick from the current models for any new integration:

- `hydra` (Hydra) - Best motion and prompt adherence.
- `griffin-hd` (Griffin) - Cinematic videos in any style, with audio, 768p.
- `forge` (Forge) - Cheapest alternative, for simple body shapes and simple actions.
- `forge-pixel` (Forge Pixel) - Best for low-res pixel art animations

Which models each action accepts (in preference order):

- sprite animation: `hydra`, `griffin-hd`, `forge`, `forge-pixel`
- motion transfer: `hydra`, `forge`, `forge-pixel`
- spritesheet editing: `hydra`, `griffin-hd`, `forge`, `forge-pixel`
- new view: `hydra`
- video generation: `griffin-hd`
- references to video: `griffin-hd`
- video editing: `griffin-hd`

**Legacy models** are still accepted so existing integrations keep working, but they are scheduled for removal - do not use them for new work:

- `hydra-plus` (Hydra+) - legacy since 2026-11-02
- `blitz` (Blitz) - legacy since 2026-09-17
- `eagle` (Eagle) - legacy since 2026-09-17
- `eagle-audio` (Eagle with Audio) - legacy since 2026-09-17
- `tango` (Tango) - legacy since 2026-09-17

Each generation endpoint lists its own models, rates and durations in its `model` parameter description.

## Timeout
Generation requests return `202` immediately (see below) and hold no connection open while the work runs. If you opt into a synchronous response with `async: false`, include a generous timeout (at least 20 minutes): the call is held for at most 15 minutes, and past that you receive `202` with the job instead of an error and resume with `GET /assets/jobs/{id}`.

## Documentation
`GET /docs/search?query=...` searches Ludo's feature guides with a plain-language
question and returns the few sections that answer it (each names a `doc` and
`section`). `GET /docs` lists every document and section, and `GET /docs?doc=...`
reads one in full. Both are free (no credits) and rate-limited: 60 requests per 5 minutes
and 1000 per day for search, 150 per 5 minutes for reading. Read the relevant guide before
your first call to a generator: it explains modes, models, margins and known limitations.

## Async Usage
Generation endpoints are asynchronous: you submit the work, get a job id back, and
collect the result when it is ready. Nothing is held open while a GPU runs.

1. **Submit** the generation. The API responds immediately with
   `202 { id, status: "queued" }`.
2. **Poll** `GET /assets/jobs/{id}` until `status` is `succeeded` or `failed`.
   Non-terminal responses carry `poll_after_ms` - wait at least that long before the
   next poll. Better still, long-poll: `GET /assets/jobs/{id}?wait=30` holds the
   request up to 30 s (max 60) and returns the moment the job finishes.
3. **Read** `result` - it is exactly the response documented for that operation. On a
   failure, read `error` instead.

`GET /assets/jobs` lists your recent jobs, and `DELETE /assets/jobs/{id}` cancels one
that has not finished yet (credits are refunded).

Job-status endpoints are rate-limited to 150 requests per 5 minutes per API key; a
`429` carries `Retry-After`. Each account may have up to 50 generations queued or
running at once via the API; a request beyond that returns `429` (code
`PENDING_JOBS_LIMIT`) - wait for jobs to finish, then submit again.

### Synchronous responses (deprecated)
Passing `async: false` in the payload opts into a synchronous response: the call blocks
until the result is ready and returns it as the response body. This is deprecated, but
the opt-out is permanent and stays supported.

Synchronous calls run on the same queue: the response carries an `X-Ludo-Job-Id`
header, and if the job is still running after 15 minutes you receive `202` with the job
instead of an error - resume with `GET /assets/jobs/{id}`.

The legacy `request_id` + `GET /assets/{type}/results` flow keeps working unchanged.

### Legacy results endpoints
Each asset type still has a results endpoint:
- `GET /assets/images/results` - images
- `GET /assets/sprites/results` - spritesheets
- `GET /assets/videos/results` - videos
- `GET /assets/audio/results` - audio
- `GET /assets/3d-models/results` - 3D models

Results are available for 7 days and return the 100 most recent API-generated assets. The `request_id` query parameter is optional - omit it to list all recent results.

## Directional Sprites
Directional Sprites render one 3D model as sprites seen from up to 8 directions that line up. The calls go in this order:
1. *(Optional)* `POST /assets/3d-model/image` (create3DModelImage): a character image from a `prompt`, or your own `image` redrawn as a 3D render (the prompt then says what to change). Call again for another try.
2. `POST /assets/3d-model` (create3DModel) with that image and `rig: true`, for a rigged GLB. A model you already have can be rigged with `POST /assets/3d-model/rig` (rigModel).
   *(Optional)* accessories - a sword, a gun, a shield, a helmet, a backpack: an item GLB (create3DModel, no rig) held by a bone of the model. `POST /assets/sprite/directional-accessory-fit` (fitDirectionalAccessory, free) fits one automatically for its `kind` and answers previews, numeric `checks` and a `placement`; call it again with `size`, `move` and `turn` (relative to the automatic fit) until it looks right. Then `POST /assets/sprite/directional-accessories` (attachDirectionalAccessories, free) with every item's placement: its `model_url` is the model holding them, to pass as `model` below.
3. *(Optional)* an animation, at most one: a `preset_id` from `GET /assets/sprite/animation-presets` (listAnimationPresets), an `animation_id` from `POST /assets/animation` (createAnimation, a move generated from a text prompt) or `GET /assets/animations` (listMyAnimations), or an `animation_url` made for this model by animate3DModelPreset or animate3DModel. With none, the sprites are a still pose.
4. `GET /assets/sprite/directional-styles` (listDirectionalSpriteStyles, free): pick a `style_id` and its `style_params`.
5. `POST /assets/sprite/directional-preview` (previewDirectionalSprites, free and synchronous): check the look from the directions you want. One preview at a time; a newer one cancels yours.
6. `POST /assets/sprite/directional` (createDirectionalSprites) for one spritesheet per direction, or `POST /assets/sprite/directional-stills` (createDirectionalStills) for one large image per direction. Pass the GLB as `model`, the animation, the style and up to 8 `directions`.

Read the full guide with `GET /docs?doc=directional-sprites`.

## Asset URL Expiration
All generated asset URLs (images, spritesheets, videos, audio, 3D models) are temporary and expire after **7 days**. If you need to keep an asset, download it before it expires.

## Request Format
- Use `Content-Type: application/json` for all requests
- All responses are returned in JSON format

## Credits
Each API call consumes credits from your account. The credit cost varies by endpoint and is documented in each endpoint's description.

> **Note:** All API requests consume credits, even if your subscription includes unlimited credits for the web application. Check your account dashboard for your current API credit balance.

Generate game-art images from a text prompt alone, selecting an image_type (e.g. sprite) and optionally art_style, perspective, and aspect_ratio. The job result is an array of image results, each with a url; request n (1-8) to control how many variations come back. Use createImage to make new images from scratch; use generateWithStyle to match a reference image's art style, editImage to modify an existing image, and removeBackground to cut out a subject. Pass an optional request_id to tag the results so you can retrieve them later via listGenerations (type image). Requires an API key (user scope). post.description:
Animate a static sprite into a spritesheet driven by a motion text prompt (image-to-spritesheet): supply an initial_image (URL or base64) plus a motion_prompt like "walking" or "attack slash", and optionally a final_image to interpolate between a start and end frame. Describe the motion exactly and unambiguously, but do not over-describe it: an action the model already knows is one phrase, not a sequence of steps, and the character, art style, background and camera come from the image, not the prompt. For animations driven by up to three keyframes (including a middle frame), use animateSpriteKeyframes instead. The job result is a single sprite result: `spritesheet_url` (the sheet image), `video_url` (an mp4 of the animation - pass it as `video` to transferMotion or as `spritesheet_video_url` to createSpriteAudio; editSpritesheet takes `spritesheet_url`), `num_frames`/`num_cols`/`num_rows` (the grid layout), and, when requested, `gif_url`, `individual_frame_urls` and `spritesheet_with_background_url`. The hydra and hydra-plus models also return `audio_url`, a sound effect for the animation - there is no need to call createSpriteAudio afterwards; forge and forge-pixel produce no audio. The chosen model must support sprite animation and the duration must be valid for it; incompatible model/duration combinations return HTTP 400. Credits are held for the duration you requested when the job is accepted; the final charge is rate × seconds of video generated (legacy models keep their minimum charge), never more than for the duration you requested, and the difference (or everything, if the job fails or is cancelled) is refunded. The returned sheet is then trimmed to its best loop and can run slightly shorter than the video; that trim is not deducted. Choosing a tool: animateSprite (this one) when you can describe the motion in text; transferMotion when you want an exact motion copied from a reference video or one of the named presets from listAnimationPresets (e.g. a standard walk or attack cycle); generatePose first when the source image is not yet in the pose the animation should start from. Omit `model` to run on hydra (the default) - see the `model` field for the per-model rates. Pass an optional request_id to tag the result so you can locate it later via listGenerations (type spritesheet). Requires an API key (user scope). get.description: Browse or read Ludo's own documentation in full - how to choose a sprite animation mode, when to use Generate Before / Generate After, how margins behave, which model suits a job, and each generator's known limitations. To answer a specific question, call searchDocs first: it returns just the sections that match. Use getDocs to see what documentation exists, or to read a whole document or named sections. This is the same documentation the Ludo web app shows its users, so it occasionally describes buttons rather than parameters; the substance applies to the API and MCP surfaces just the same. To browse, call it with NO parameters to get a table of contents - every document with its id, label and section titles, and no bodies - then call it again with `doc` (and optionally `sections`) to read only what you need. Fetching a whole document can return tens of thousands of characters, so prefer naming the sections, using titles copied from the table of contents. Section titles match ignoring case, spacing and punctuation: when only some requested titles exist you receive those sections plus `unmatched_sections` and `available_sections`, and when none exist (or `doc` is unknown) the call returns 400 listing the valid values so you can retry once. This is a free discovery endpoint: it does not charge credits and does not queue a job. Requires an API key (user scope).

get.description:
List your generation history - everything you have generated, through the API or in the Ludo web studio - most recent first. This is a free read-only lookup (no credits, no generation); it does not create anything. Pick a media `type` (image, spritesheet, video, audio, or 3d) and optionally narrow by free-text `search` (matched against tags, prompts and the other text on the asset), `source`, a `date_from`/`date_to` range (unix seconds), or the `request_id` you passed when you generated. Results are paginated with `page_size` (default 20, max 100) and 1-based `page_number`, and come back as an object: `items` (this page), plus `page`, `page_size` and `has_more`. Page until `has_more` is false rather than until you get a short page. `has_more` is computed by reading one row beyond the page, so it costs no extra query; there is deliberately no total count.

`source` selects the surface an item came from: `api` returns only your API/MCP generations, `web` only your web-studio ones, `all` (the default) both. API-originated items expire 7 days after creation - their files live under a lifecycle-pruned storage prefix - so `source=api` never returns anything older than 7 days, while web items are kept indefinitely and are not time-bounded. API-originated results expire after 7 days - download anything you want to retain. (Assets can be kept permanently from the Ludo web app.) Each item carries an `id`, its generation-history id, which identifies the item across these listings. Every item also carries `type`, echoing the media type you asked for; on audio items the kind of audio (sfx, music, speech) is reported as `audio_type` so it does not collide with it.

This lists work that has already FINISHED. To follow a generation that is still queued or running, poll getApiJob with the job id you were given instead. Requires an API key (user scope).

loop.description: Trim the animation at the beginning or end to create a seamless loop. Not guaranteed to produce a perfect loop.

Exporting larger than the input image adds no detail: do not pick a size above the input's own resolution, and 0 or -1 gain nothing on inputs under 512 px. Every bit of margin is resolution taken from the sprite, so keep it as tight as the motion allows - about 0.15 - and go higher only for motion that extends sideways (sword slashes, punches) or if the sprite gets cut off. Supplying a value selects margin_ratio_mode "manual" unless margin_ratio_mode is set explicitly; overrides the legacy margin_ratio on this axis.

Every bit of margin is resolution taken from the sprite, so keep it as tight as the motion allows - about 0.15 - and go higher only for motion that extends up or down (jumps) or if the sprite gets cut off. Supplying a value selects margin_ratio_mode "manual" unless margin_ratio_mode is set explicitly; overrides the legacy margin_ratio on this axis.

The model always generates on a canvas of the same size, so any margin is canvas the sprite does not fill: the more margin, the lower the resolution and detail of the sprite. "auto" (default, recommended) trims and centers the sprite and picks a margin suited to the motion. "manual" uses margin_ratio_horizontal / margin_ratio_vertical; keep them as tight as the motion allows (about 0.15) and raise only the axis the motion needs. "none" animates the input exactly as framed, with no trimming and no margin added, so the input must already have suitable margins: a sprite touching the edges gets its limbs, weapons and effects cut off as soon as it moves, and an image that is mostly empty space yields a small, low-detail sprite. "none" is the way to keep a deliberately off-center sprite (e.g. a character at the left edge firing a beam to the right), but results can be unpredictable. Do not use "none" to make the spritesheet line up with the input image - use frame_size -9 (True Size) for that; it works with any margin mode. TransferMotionPayload.description: Payload for transferring motion from a video, an animation preset or a generated animation onto a static sprite image, producing an animated spritesheet.

image.description: The static sprite to animate, as a URL or base64 image. Ideally an image generated with the "sprite", "sprite-vfx" or "ui_asset" image type.

video.description: URL of the video to use as motion source - the `video_url` of a spritesheet from animateSprite, or your own clip. Videos up to 4 seconds work best. One of `video`, `preset_id` and `animation_id` must be provided (the last two with `perspective` + `direction`); when a video is sent with one of them, the preset or animation is used. A video more than twice as long as `duration` gets heavily compressed and the motion turns rushed - trim it to the part you want, or raise `duration`.

preset_id.description: ID of an animation preset to use instead of a video URL. Use listAnimationPresets to list available presets. When using a preset, `perspective` and `direction` are required. At most one of preset_id and animation_id.

animation_id.description: The id of one of the account's generated animations (from createAnimation or listMyAnimations) to use instead of a video URL or a preset. An animation can be seen from any view, so `perspective` and `direction` are required, as with a preset - pick the view the sprite is drawn from. At most one of preset_id and animation_id; an animation that is not on the account returns HTTP 404.

mirror.description: With preset_id or animation_id, play the move on the other side, left and right swapped (a slash with the left arm from one with the right). Not available with a `video`, where it returns HTTP 400. Off unless set to true.

direction.description: Where the camera stands around the character for the animation preset or animation. Required with `preset_id` or `animation_id`.

perspective.description: Camera perspective the preset or animation is seen from, by id (the `perspectives` list of listAnimationPresets, the same set for every preset): high = tactical steep top-down, horizon = side view at eye level, isometric = diagonal top-down with depth, low = hero low angle, top = directly overhead. Required when using a preset. Unrelated to the `perspective` of createImage, which is a free-text art direction.

frames.description: Maximum number of frames in the output spritesheet. Allow about one second of duration per 16 frames - above that the model may not be able to produce them all (64 frames needs a duration of at least 4). The result can have fewer frames when the duration is short or bad frames were removed.

frame_size.description: Size of the sprite in pixels, not of the frame: it sets how big the character is drawn in the exported sheet, and each frame also holds the space around the sprite, so frames come out larger than this value. 0 is maximum resolution. Exporting larger than the input image adds no detail: do not pick a size above the input's own resolution, and 0 gains nothing on inputs under 512 px. True Size is not available here: the image is not the first frame of the result, so there is nothing to align to.

loop.description: Trim the animation at the beginning or end to create a seamless loop.

crop.description: Crop sprite frames to fit content. Results in smaller spritesheets but inconsistent frame sizes across different animations.

margin_ratio.description: Deprecated: prefer margin_ratio_horizontal / margin_ratio_vertical. Amount of padding around the sprite as a ratio (0.0 to 1.0). Sets both axes to this value. A per-axis value, when also given, overrides this for that axis. Defaults to 0.15 when no margin value is given at all.

margin_ratio_horizontal.description: Horizontal padding around the sprite as a ratio (0.0 to 1.0). Every bit of margin is resolution taken from the sprite, so keep it as tight as the motion allows - about 0.15 - and go higher only for motion that extends sideways (sword slashes, punches) or if the sprite gets cut off. Overrides the legacy margin_ratio on this axis.

margin_ratio_vertical.description: Vertical padding around the sprite as a ratio (0.0 to 1.0). Every bit of margin is resolution taken from the sprite, so keep it as tight as the motion allows - about 0.15 - and go higher only for motion that extends up or down (jumps) or if the sprite gets cut off. Overrides the legacy margin_ratio on this axis.

margin_ratio_mode.description: How the sprite is framed for generation. Defaults to "manual" (0.15 on each axis when no margin value is given); transfer motion has no "auto". The model always generates on a canvas of the same size, so any margin is canvas the sprite does not fill: the more margin, the lower the resolution and detail of the sprite. Keep the margins tight - about 0.15 - and raise only the axis the motion needs. "none" animates the image exactly as framed, so it must already have suitable margins (not touching the edges, not mostly empty space); an off-center sprite can give unpredictable results. Sending "none" together with a margin value fails with HTTP 400 (the value would be ignored).

gif.description: When true, generates an animated GIF from the spritesheet and returns it in gif_url. Disabled by default to reduce response time.

individual_frames.description: When true, extracts each frame from the spritesheet as an individual image and returns the URLs in individual_frame_urls.

spritesheet_with_background.description: When true, also returns the spritesheet with background intact (before background removal). Useful for manually fixing background removal issues. The with-background spritesheet URL will be in spritesheet_with_background_url.

use_pixel_grid.description: Use the animation's pixel grid if one is detected. Defaults to true. true: when Ludo detects a pixel grid with confidence, the sheet is packed on it (logical pixels, scaled up by whole blocks); when none is detected, this has no effect. false: always pack as ordinary art, for when the detected grid is wrong for your asset (for example a smooth sprite coming back as coarse blocks). Ignored for forge-pixel animations, which are always packed on their grid.

delivery.description: How the line is said, e.g. "angry, shouting" or "whispering, out of breath" (max 50 characters). Only for the first-name voices (e.g. "Rachel"); a descriptive voice returns HTTP 400 - use emotion instead.

language.description: Language of the speech. Each voice family supports its own list of languages; "auto" detects it from the text.

request_id.description: Optional client-provided identifier, unique per request. Re-sending the same request_id returns the existing job instead of generating again. Also usable as the request_id filter of listGenerations.

async.description: Defaults to true: the call returns 202 immediately with a job id to poll with getApiJob. Set false for a synchronous response (deprecated but supported): the call then blocks until the result is ready.

items.description: This page of results, newest first.

page.description: The 1-based page number these items came from.

page_size.description: The page size actually applied (your page_size, clamped to 1-100).

has_more.description: Whether at least one more page exists after this one. Page until this is false rather than until you get a short page.

prompt.description: The prompt the source image was generated from (text-to-3D). Absent for a model made from your own image.

source_image_url.description: URL of the image the model was built from (the generated concept image, or the image you sent).

model.description: The image-to-3D model that made the model, prop or hero (create3DModel `model`), kept through rigging. Absent for uploaded models and for models made before Nov 10 2026.

CreateUploadPayload.description: Payload for starting a file upload.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the file. Fixed for the upload; the stored file is served with it.

size.description: Exact size of the file in bytes (at most 15MB). The PUT to upload_url must send exactly this many bytes.

upload_url.description: Single-use URL to PUT the file's bytes to, with no Authorization header.

file_url.description: Public URL of the file once the PUT succeeds. Pass it to any field that accepts a URL. Deleted 7 days after upload.

mime_type.description: The MIME type the file is stored and served with.

size.description: The exact number of bytes the PUT must send.

currency.description: Currency of every price, e.g. usd.

plans.description: Cheapest first. Free Trial comes first and has no prices.

rules.description: What to know before advising a user to pay, each with a stable id.

costs.description: What each priced API operation (MCP tool) costs.

available.description: Credits generations can spend right now.

plan_credits.description: The plan's credits for the current cycle.

extra.description: Credits from top-ups and grants, on top of the plan.

resets_at.description: When the plan credits refill (unix seconds).

team_pool.description: The balance is a team's shared pool.

grace_until.description: Set when the subscription ended; remaining credits stay spendable until then (unix seconds).

auto_topup.description: Null for team members; the team owner manages auto top-up.

threshold.description: An automatic top-up is bought when available credits drop below this.

credits.description: Credits bought on each automatic top-up.

billing_url.description: Web page to buy credits, change plan or change auto top-up.

ApiFeedbackPayload.description: Payload for reporting a bug, limitation or missing capability to Ludo

category.description: bug - the API errored, a job failed or got stuck, or a response did not match the documentation; limitation - the API does not support a parameter, operation or format you needed; feature_request - a new API capability you would like; praise - something that worked well; other - any other API issue. Generated content that looks wrong or does not match the prompt is a model limitation, not a bug: do not report it. A limitation the docs already describe (check with searchDocs) is known: do not report it.

message.description: What you were trying to do, what happened, and what would have helped.

operation.description: The operation the feedback is about, e.g. animateSprite.

job_id.description: The id of the job the feedback is about. Same as a one-item job_ids.

job_ids.description: The ids of the jobs the feedback is about (returned by each generation call; also in getApiJob and listApiJobs). Send them whenever a job is involved: every job that shows the problem, plus the one that worked if you are comparing.

agent.description: The agent or app sending it, e.g. Claude Code.

ModelLineup.description: Which models to use. Present on the table of contents only (no `doc` parameter).

legacy.description: Legacy models: still accepted for existing integrations but scheduled for removal. Do not use them for new work.

id.description: Stable document id, e.g. sprite-generator - pass it back as the `doc` parameter

label.description: Human-readable document name, e.g. Sprite Generator

doc.description: Document id, e.g. sprite-generator - pass it to getDocs as `doc`

label.description: Human-readable document name, e.g. Sprite Generator

section.description: Section title - pass it to getDocs in `sections`

relevance.description: Match score 0-1; only results at or above 0.6 are returned

content.description: Full markdown body of the section, as getDocs would return it. Request and response schemas for each tool are in the tool definitions, not in these sections.

pixel.description: Whether the style is pixel art.

settings.description: The style's settings: each has a name (its key in style_params), label, description, kind (choice, bool or color), options ({label, value}) and default.

advanced_settings.description: Finer settings, described the same way.

direction.description: The direction this preview is seen from.

frame_urls.description: The preview's frames as images, in order (one for a still model). Kept for 7 days.

direction.description: The direction this sheet is seen from.

num_frames.description: Number of frames in the spritesheet.

num_cols.description: Columns in the frame grid. Frames run left-to-right, top-to-bottom.

num_rows.description: Rows in the frame grid. The last row may be only partly filled.

fps.description: The frame rate the sheet plays at.

loop.description: Whether the animation loops: the loop you asked for, else the animation's own. false is a one-shot (a jump, a death) that should play once in an engine.

normal_map_url.description: The spritesheet's normal map (lossless WebP, same layout as the sheet), when save_normals was true and the map could be made.

direction.description: The direction this image is seen from.

normal_map_url.description: The image's normal map (lossless WebP), when save_normals was true and the map could be made.

DirectionalAccessoryAxes.description: Along or about the character's own axes: forward (where it faces), up, and out (away from the body's middle for an item in a hand; to the character's left on the head, back or hips).

DirectionalAccessoryPlacement.description: Where an item is held, exactly. Pass it unchanged to attachDirectionalAccessories.

DirectionalAccessoryChecks.description: Numbers about the fit, from sampled vertices in the model's rest pose: a quick way to tell a fine fit from a clearly wrong one.

sink.description: How deep the item goes into the body, in % of the character's height (95th percentile of its vertices). Near 0 is right; an item in a hand is checked against the body without that hand.

inside.description: The share of the item's vertices under the body's surface, in %.

grip_gap.description: For an item held by a grip in a hand (not a shield) - how far its grip is from the palm, in % of the character's height. Near 0 is in the fist.

through.description: For an item on the head - the share of the head's vertices (hair and all) poking out through it, in %: for a helmet, where it covers the head; for a hat, under the hat only (ears standing beside it are not counted). A helmet draws in what would poke through it (hair, ear tips) when it is put on, so near 0 is expected.

item.description: The item, as a URL or base64-encoded GLB file, as sent to fitDirectionalAccessory. Up to 30MB.

name.description: What the item is, in words; its name when saved.

placement.description: The placement fitDirectionalAccessory returned for this item, unchanged. Without it, the item goes at the automatic fit plus kind/point/bone/size/move/turn/flip/grip, as fitDirectionalAccessory would put it.

preset_id.description: Set when the clip came from the preset library (retargeting) rather than a text prompt.

animation_id.description: Set when the clip was retargeted from one of the account's animations - its id, as createAnimation and listMyAnimations give it.

mirror.description: True when the preset or motion was mirrored (left and right swapped).

id.description: The animation's id. Pass it as `animation_id` to animate3DModelPreset, createDirectionalSprites, previewDirectionalSprites or transferMotion.

name.description: A kebab-case name for the move (e.g. overhead-two-handed-sword-slash-to-the-ground). It names the clip in 3D animations made from the animation, and can be changed in the web app.

prompt.description: The prompt the animation was generated from.

caption.description: The description the motion model was given - the rewritten prompt, or the prompt itself with augment_prompt false.

loop.description: Whether the animation is a seamless cycle.

preview_url.description: An mp4 of the animation on a mannequin, seen from the low camera facing SW, at real speed. It stays with the animation and does not expire.

created_at.description: When the animation was generated (unix seconds).

id.description: Generation-history id of this item, identifying it across these listings. API-originated results expire after 7 days - download anything you want to retain. (Assets can be kept permanently from the Ludo web app.)

type.description: The media type of this item, echoing the requested `type`.

created_at.description: When the item was generated (unix seconds).

url.description: image / video / audio: URL to the generated file.

duration.description: video / audio / spritesheet: duration in seconds.

audio_type.description: audio only: the kind of audio (sfx, music, speech). Named `audio_type` here, not `type`, because `type` reports the media type on every item.

audio_url.description: spritesheet only: URL of the sheet's sound effect (MP3 or WAV; the extension says which), when it has one.

num_cols.description: spritesheet only: columns in the frame grid. Frames run left-to-right, top-to-bottom.

num_rows.description: spritesheet only: rows in the frame grid. The last row may be only partly filled.

out_of_frame.description: spritesheet only: true when Ludo detected the sprite running past the frame's edges, so parts of it are cut off. A hint; editSpritesheet edit_mode "outpaint" extends the frame. A larger margin can't help when the input image itself is cut at that edge.

bad_loop.description: spritesheet only: true when Ludo detected that the animation doesn't loop cleanly. A hint; editSpritesheet edit_mode "fix_loop" generates a new clip to repair it, so use it only when this is true.

frame_width.description: spritesheet only: width in pixels of one cell of the sheet. Every frame is the same size. Absent on older spritesheets.

frame_height.description: spritesheet only: height in pixels of one cell of the sheet. Absent on older spritesheets.

pixel_block.description: spritesheet only: pixel art only, absent otherwise. How many sheet pixels make up one art pixel, so the art is frame_width / pixel_block pixels wide. Snap or scale by this to keep the pixels crisp. On a true-size export the block grid can be shifted from the frame's top-left corner.

loop_score.description: spritesheet only: 0 to 1, how similar the last frame played is to the first. bad_loop is exactly loop_score < 0.7. Absent on older spritesheets.

loop_detected.description: spritesheet only: true when a loop was requested and the sheet holds one full cycle: it was found in the video, or the final keyframe was the same image as the first. false means the whole clip was packed, ending wherever the video ended. Absent on older spritesheets.

out_of_frame_edges.description: spritesheet only: the borders the sprite is cut off on, which tells you where to add margin. Empty when nothing is cut off; out_of_frame is true exactly when it is non-empty. Absent on older spritesheets.

model_url.description: 3d only: URL to the generated model file.

model.description: image: the id of the model that generated or edited the image. Absent on older images. 3d: the image-to-3D model that made the model, prop or hero (create3DModel `model`), kept through rigging; absent for uploaded models and for models made before Nov 10 2026.

prompt.description: image: the prompt as the model received it. With augment_prompt on, this is the rewritten prompt, not the one you sent. 3d: the prompt the source image was generated from (text-to-3D); absent for a model made from your own image.

source_image_url.description: 3d only: URL of the image the model was built from (the generated concept image, or the image you sent). A text-to-3D concept image saved without a model yet has this and `prompt`, and no `model_url`.

api_access.description: Whether the API, MCP and CLI generation work on this plan.

credits_per_month.description: Credits each month, for the whole team on Studio. Null on Free Trial.

credits_at_signup.description: Free Trial only - its credits, given once.

queue_concurrency.description: How many generations run at once.

brackets.description: The price at each bracket, in cents. An amount between two brackets is priced on the straight line between them.

operation.description: The API operationId, which is also the MCP tool name.

billing.description: Where the user subscribes, changes plan and buys credits.

CurrentModelsByAction.description: Per credit action, the current model codenames in preference order. Pick from these for new work.

features.description: Credit actions the model still accepts; empty once fully retired.

style_params.description: The style's settings as rendered, by name.

animation_id.description: The account's animation (from createAnimation) the render played, when it was given one.

mirror.description: True when the preset or motion was mirrored (left and right swapped).

amount.description: Price per interval, in currency units (50 = $50).

per_month.description: Annual prices only - the price divided by 12.

credits_granted.description: Credits per interval. Annual plans grant the whole year at once.
